paper_metadata.title: A quantum generative adversarial network for distributions

summary: This paper presents a fully quantum generative adversarial network (QuGAN) for learning a discretized SVI implied-volatility distribution on 24 grid points over [-1,1]. The described setup uses 4 qubits for the distribution, 3 ancilla qubits in the discriminator, and 13 trainable parameters in the extracted configuration, with training reported as 9 discriminator steps and 1 generator step per epoch; no classical benchmark or practical speedup is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Fully quantum generative adversarial network (QuGAN) for learning a discretized SVI implied-volatility-derived distribution in finance, trained with a quantum discriminator and quantum generator using IBM Qiskit.

algorithm.variant: fully connected quantum generative adversarial network (QuGAN) with quantum discriminator and quantum generator
algorithm.ansatz: custom quantum perceptron/discriminator built from QPE-based inner product and activation circuits; custom entangled generator built from RY, cRY, and X gates

hyperparameters.epochs: repeated training loop; exact number not reported

algorithm.parameter_initialization: discriminator weights initialized from Uniform[-1,1]; generator weights initialized from [0,2]

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The target SVI density is discretized on a uniform grid over [-1,1] with 24 points and converted into binary form; the generated distribution is represented as a wavefunction over computational basis states.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Min-max GAN objective: min_G max_D V(D,G) = D_w(0|0_target) - D_w(0|0), where D_w(0|0_target) is the probability of labeling real data as real and D_w(0|0) is the probability of fooling the discriminator.

problem_instance.description: Learning a discrete approximation of the SVI-implied probability distribution of log stock returns for a financial volatility modeling task.

dataset_specification.description: SVI parameters given in Eq. (4.6); distribution normalized on [-1,1] and discretized on a uniform grid with 24 points

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute SVI total implied variance and density, normalize on [-1,1], discretize uniformly, then convert discretized probabilities to binary representation for quantum state preparation
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Training monitored using fidelity and Kullback-Leibler divergence; results shown over training epochs

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretization of the SVI density and binary encoding of probabilities
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute fidelity and KL divergence from measured/generated distributions

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: training curves shown; convergence discussed qualitatively

speedup_claims.conditions: claimed in the introduction for quantum GANs in general; not experimentally demonstrated in this paper
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this as a general motivation and does not provide a formal asymptotic proof or benchmark against a classical baseline in the reported experiment.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not established; the paper reports a 4-qubit discretized target distribution with 3 ancilla qubits and 13 trainable parameters in the described setup, but no asymptotic resource analysis or benchmarked crossover point.
